svg.desc: Two controlled changes separate a cup's position relative to gaze from its position relative to the hand. A: the eyes rotate with head, hand and cup fixed; the cup's offset from the fovea changes while the hand-to-cup vector does not. B: the hand start changes with head, eyes and cup fixed; the hand-to-cup vector changes while the offset from the fovea does not. C: retinal, eye-position and hand-position signals jointly influence one mixed population whose activity differs across the four situations (schematic).

g.text: Eyes move; head, hand, and cup stay fixed
Hand start moves; head, eyes, and cup stay fixed
Target and body-state signals jointly shape population activity
